method: One inch is exactly 25.4 mm, and the CSS absolute-length table fixes the rest: 1 in = 96 px = 72 pt = 6 pc, 1 mm = 1/10 cm, and 1 Q = 1/40 cm, so 1 in = 101.6 Q. A twip is one twentieth of a point, or 1/1440 in. Every entry is converted to inches and back out, so the eight units agree exactly with one another; the only rounding is in the display, to four significant digits, with a billionth added before rounding so a binary product that should sit on a decimal half rounds up rather than down. Sizes are accepted from 0.1 to 20,000 pt (about 0.035 mm to 7.06 m), which spans footnote sizes through billboard type, and the headline always reports points. The continental Didot point of about 0.376 mm and the 12-point cicero are a different system whose exact value varied by country, so they are deliberately not converted; leading, tracking, optical scaling and rasterising type at a print resolution are also out of scope. Everything runs in the browser, so nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere.

sources.title: CSS Values and Units Module Level 4, section 6.2 Absolute Lengths: 1in = 2.54cm = 96px, 1pc = 1/6 in, 1pt = 1/72 in, 1px = 1/96 in, 1Q = 1/40 cm
Twip: a twentieth of a point, or 1/1440 of an inch
